chapter: War years, Decca records and La Conga
title: Piano chair: Varona, Joe Loco and Jose Curbelo
summary: Frank Ayala left for the army, Varona was unreliable, and Jose Curbelo often sat in; Mario helped Curbelo start his own band.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: ....but before Joe Loco came, everytime Varona didn't show up, Jose Curbelo took his place.
Yeah, he is a great pianist.

As a matter of fact, that's when the relation and we was - were so grateful of his - the part that he took in replacing Varona, that Mario helped him tremendously to organize his band and, as a matter of fact, we - in that particular time, Jack Harris' band was the one to play the

show, so Mario told Jack Harris: "Why don't you give a two-week notice to your orchestra because we are losing clientele", because they go to the Havana Madrid. They have two latin bands, so when the show is over, or when the show started, the people go to the Chateau Madrid and stayed over there. So we losing about a hundred people a day, that would be five thousand, fifty-two hundred a year, and you know how the business men, and he was a good business man......
....he got the - black and white and said: "Mario, you are right, who you prefer to be the second man or to play the dances"?, and he say: "Jose Curbelo."
Okay, let me clarify one thing here, Frank Gilberto Ayala was the first pianist with the Machito orchestra, right?
You lost him when he went into the army, right?
How long did Varona last with the band?
Maybe six months, the time that I spent in the army.
Okay, all right. Now, during that time period, how many times would you say Curbelo sat in
About three or four times a week.
And he used to read your charts and everything.
Oh yes - no, no, he is a great pianist.
